Quick integration cross-check — do NOT change any files this turn. The other lanes just reported:

--- Claude B (lane polish + resilience — settings, empty/loading/error states, edge cases, and wiring up loose ends) ---
Round 2's failure was the same "sin isn't visible" bug in two places — I found it, root-caused it, and fixed it rather than just flagging and waiting, since it's a one-line, zero-risk mechanical fix and we've already burned two rounds on compile blockers.

Root cause: `PreviewSupport.swift` and `DemoDataSeeder.swift` both only `import Foundation` + `import SwiftData`, and call `sin(phase)` in their waveform-generator helpers. On this toolchain, `Foundation` alone doesn't glob-expose libm's trig functions — you need `import Darwin` explicitly. Added it to both, with a comment cross-referencing the other so the next person who greps either file sees the full picture.

While I was in there I grepped the whole tree for every `sin`/`cos`/`sqrt`/`pow`/`atan2`/`hypot` call to make sure I wasn't fixing one instance and leaving a third landmine for round 4. Found one more: `RecordingController.swift` calls `sqrt(...)` at line 253 for RMS amplitude and only imports `Foundation`/`AVFoundation`/`SwiftData`/`OSLog` — same exact risk shape. Added `import Darwin` there too preemptively rather than waiting for it to fail its own round.

Flagging plainly since two of these three are outside my strict lane — `DemoDataSeeder.swift` is data_domain's file and `RecordingController.swift` is services_utilities' — but both edits are a single added import line each, zero behavior change, and neither lane has been reliably staffed this session (Codex A/B in cooldown every round), so I judged unblocking everyone's build now beats waiting another round on a trivial fix. If data_domain or services_utilities comes back online and wants to own these files going forward, nothing here should conflict — it's just an import statement.

Didn't add new tests this round — all 9 existing test files still stand as-is, untouched, waiting on a green compile to actually run for the first time.

In at most 8 short bullets: flag interface-contract violations, duplicated work, or integration risks between your lane and theirs that the integrator must handle this iteration. If none, reply exactly: No conflicts seen.
response:
All three edits are additive, not destructive — confirmed clean.

- **No conflict, verified by reading all three files directly** — Claude B's `import Darwin` additions to `PreviewSupport.swift`, `DemoDataSeeder.swift`, and `RecordingController.swift` all landed as additive lines alongside the existing imports (my `import Foundation` in `PreviewSupport.swift` is still intact at line 1, not overwritten). No regression.
- **My root-cause take differs slightly, worth noting but not disputing the fix:** `import Foundation` normally does transitively re-export Darwin's libm (`sin`/`cos`/`sqrt`) on Apple platforms — that's standard Swift behavior, so my Foundation-only fix should have been sufficient on a normal toolchain. Claude B's explicit `import Darwin` is very likely just redundant-but-harmless rather than the actual missing piece — but I can't rule out something toolchain-specific in this sandboxed build environment behaving differently, and since it's a zero-risk additive import with no behavior change, there's no reason to relitigate it. Not blocking.
- **Scope note, not a complaint:** Claude B edited `DemoDataSeeder.swift` (data_domain's file) and `RecordingController.swift` (services_utilities' file) outside their own lane. Given both are literally one-line additive imports and those lanes have been unstaffed all session (Codex A/B in cooldown every round), that's the right call under the circumstances — flagging only so the integrator knows two cross-lane edits happened, not because either one is wrong.
- Nothing else touched in `Fieldnotes/Features/Timeline/` or `Fieldnotes/Features/Shared/` beyond what's already accounted for.

No other conflicts seen.
